We are looking for a PhD candidate for our new RWTH-based Collaborative Research Center (CRC 1769) on Polymer Mechanochemistry!

The project, "Mechanochemical Degradation with High Selectivity Steered by Polymer Architecture," aims to develop macromolecules with programmable and tunable mechanochemical degradability. It is based on the hypothesis that polymer topology governs the distribution and concentration of mechanical forces within macromolecular networks, thereby enabling the selective activation of mechanophores embedded in polymer chains.
To test this hypothesis, we will synthesize libraries of polymers with distinct topologies and precisely controlled distributions of mechanosensitive bonds. The mechanochemical degradation of these macromolecules will be investigated with respect to molecular size, internal structure, ultrasound parameters, monomer type, and the structure of the resulting degradation products. The resulting structure–reactivity relationships will be established and leveraged to tailor the mechanical properties of polymers across different architectural frameworks.
